item.title: Is Audrey Hobert the Most Honest Voice in Pop?
item.description: The rising pop star talks songwriting with her BFF Gracie Abrams, knowing when to log off and the difference between being weird (yes!) and awkward (no way).
item.dc:creator: Jon Caramanica, Joe Coscarelli and Caroline Tompkins
item.media:credit: Caroline Tompkins for The New York Times

item.title: ‘Spiritual Jazz’ Has Turned Cozy. John Coltrane Demanded More.
item.description: The term has lately become synonymous with sonic serenity (and chic merch). But the saxophone great challenged listeners with radical honesty.
item.dc:creator: Hank Shteamer
item.media:credit: Sarah Mazzetti

item.title: Missy Mazzoli Debuts at the Metropolitan Opera With ‘Lincoln in the Bardo’
item.description: Missy Mazzoli, whose “Lincoln in the Bardo” opens at the Metropolitan Opera this fall, writes politically urgent, musically eclectic works for a new generation of operagoers.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nagourney and David Billet
item.media:credit: David Billet for The New York Times

item.title: 5 Minutes to Make You Love John Coltrane’s ‘A Love Supreme’
item.description: Ahead of John Coltrane’s centennial, listen deeply to his 1965 spiritual jazz masterpiece as Ravi Coltrane, Lalah Hathaway and other musicians and writers reflect on its legacy.
item.dc:creator: Marcus J. Moore and Giovanni Russonello

item.title: 10 Songs We’re Talking About
item.description: Riley Green measures milestones, Grand Theft Audio VI flaunts collaboration, Kate Nash chooses to shout and more.
item.dc:creator: Jon Pareles
item.media:credit: Charles Sykes/Invision, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Riley Green measures his life in footwear on “Ten Pairs of Boots,” from his new album, “That’s Just Me.”

item.title: 5 Takeaways from the ‘Jay-Z in 8’ Documentary
item.description: The rapper unpacks the lyrics to more than two dozen of his songs and shares insights into his life with Rick Rubin, in a docuseries airing on HBO.
item.dc:creator: Derrick Bryson Taylor
item.media:credit: Courtesy of HBO
item.media:description: Jay-Z unpacked some of his most famous and vulnerable verses with Rick Rubin, right.

item.title: ‘American Psycho’ Was Duncan Sheik’s Darkest Work. Was It Also His Best?
item.description: In translating synth pop to a theatrical format in the “American Psycho” musical, Sheik matched what he did with rock in the acclaimed “Spring Awakening.”
item.dc:creator: Elisabeth Vincentelli
item.media:credit: Sara Krulwich/The New York Times
item.media:description: The musical “American Psycho” had a short Broadway run in 2016 at the Gerald Schoenfeld Theater.

item.title: Duncan Sheik, Who Traded Pop Stardom for Broadway, Dies at 56
item.description: Weary of the heartthrob label after his 1996 hit “Barely Breathing,” he pivoted to musical theater and won two Tonys for composing “Spring Awakening.”
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams

item.title: San Francisco Opera Reaches Deal With Orchestra, Ending Strike
item.description: Nearly a week after opening night was canceled while patrons were in their seats, the musicians agreed to a four-year contract. The deal still needs to be ratified.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nagourney
item.media:credit: Kelsey McClellan for The New York Times
item.media:description: Further details of the agreement between the San Francisco Opera and its orchestra were not immediately released.

item.title: Kennedy Center Closure Prompts Legal Fight Over Trump-Backed Renovation
item.description: The federal judge denied a Democratic lawmaker’s request for an emergency hearing on the closure, which began on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Salwan Georges for The New York Times
item.media:description: Matt Floca, the executive director of the Kennedy Center, has said the building has serious maintenance needs, including structural steel corroded by water infiltration.

item.title: Gustavo Dudamel’s New York Era Has Begun. Try to Keep Up.
item.description: The New York Philharmonic’s season started with a barnstorming tour of Manhattan to celebrate Dudamel’s arrival as music and artistic director.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Barone and George Etheredge
item.category: Perelman, Ronald O, Performing Arts Center

item.title: It’s a Rap-Wrestling Mash-Up, Irish Style
item.description: At Clash at the Quays in Dublin, rappers and grime M.C.s trade superkicks and story lines, and the crowd goes wild.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Evans and Ellius Grace
item.media:credit: Ellius Grace for The New York Times
item.media:description: The wrestlers Rich Swann and Delsin Brooks at Clash at the Quays. The event features clashes among wrestlers and musicians.

item.title: New York Performing Arts Library Gets $60 Million Gift for Preservation
item.description: The anonymous donation, the library’s largest ever, will support digitization of archival items related to theater, dance and music.
item.dc:creator: Malia Mendez
item.category: New York Public Library for the Performing Arts

item.title: Gregor Benko, Who Resurrected a Vanished Musical World, Dies at 82
item.description: For over 60 years, he unearthed rare early piano recordings, illuminating an expressive, highly individual style that had fallen from favor.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Woolfe

item.title: Emergency Hearing Sought Over Kennedy Center Closure
item.description: After a Democratic lawmaker asked a judge to consider whether the move violates a previous court order, center officials clarified that the closure was intended to last seven days.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Zach Montague
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Salwan Georges for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Kennedy Center temporarily closed its main building to visitors on Tuesday, citing safety concerns after plaster fell from the ceiling. A federal judge has yet to approve the center’s plan to close for a two-year renovation project.

item.title: Karol G, Rosalía Are Among the Most-Nominated Artists at the 2026 Latin Grammys
item.description: Along with Ca7riel and Paco Amoroso, and Jorge Drexler, the artists each scored seven nominations for ambitious, genre-spanning projects.
item.dc:creator: Paula Mejía
item.media:credit: Mario Anzuoni/Reuters
item.media:description: Karol G’s album “Tropicoqueta” drew from styles that inspired her, including vallenatos, dembow, cumbia, reggaeton and ranchera.

item.title: Empress Of Rebuilds “Dream House” After Fire
item.description: Empress Of, the electronic musician, layered themes of instability and renewal on “Dream House,” a new album threaded with her mother’s stories about their Altadena home lost in the 2025 wildfire.
item.dc:creator: Carolina Abbott Galvão and Maiwenn Raoult
item.media:description: “I’m just really proud of the resilience of my town,” Rodriguez said of Altadena.

item.title: How Ed Sheeran’s Tour Turned Into a Clash Over Palestinians and Antisemitism
item.description: Four supporting acts dropped out of Sheeran’s tour, citing the right to free speech after the rapper Macklemore was removed over pro-Palestinian comments he had made onstage.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:credit: Kylie Cooper/Reuters
item.media:description: In a social media statement on Tuesday announcing he was dropping out of the Sheeran tour, Finneas said, “I stand with Palestine and its people.”

item.title: Oliver Jones, ‘Greatest Living Jazz Musician in Canada,’ Dies at 91
item.description: Growing up in the shadow of the piano giant Oscar Peterson, he became a jazz institution in his own right and collected an array of honors.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams
item.media:credit: Stéphane Ouzounoff/Hans Lucas, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Oliver Jones in 1994. Andy Williams, a Montreal jazz educator and radio host, said that there was “a softness, a subtlety to his playing, like a watercolor.”

item.description: Hear our critic’s picks from Remi Wolf, Tinashe, Cameron Winter and more.

item.media:description: Remi Wolf

item.title: Kennedy Center Closes Its Doors Despite a Judge’s Order
item.description: The announcement came after President Trump said he would cancel a $257 million renovation of the venue if his name is not returned to the building.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Zach Montague
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Salwan Georges for The New York Times
item.media:description: A federal judge ruled that the Kennedy Center did not have the authority to place President Trump’s name on the exterior of the building.

item.title: As ‘Annie’ Turns 50, a Revival Will Open on Broadway
item.description: A revival of the endlessly popular musical will open in the fall of 2027.
item.dc:creator: Michael Paulson
item.media:credit: Sara Krulwich/The New York Times
item.media:description: The iconic “Annie” dress, from 1977, at the Museum of Broadway. The dress was designed by Theoni V. Aldredge, who won a Tony Award for the show’s costumes.

item.title: A Nancy Pelosi-A.O.C. Drama, ‘Little Shop of Horrors’ and More Theater to Stream
item.description: This month’s picks include the “Hamilton” alum in Ossie Davis’s 1961 play, a political comedy by Mario Correa, and “Little Shop of Horrors” in high definition.

item.title: The Cellist Jeffrey Zeigler Explores His Family’s Gullah Geechee Roots
item.description: In a new multidisciplinary work, the cellist Jeffrey Zeigler explores his family’s Gullah Geechee roots in South Carolina with a host of collaborators.
item.dc:creator: Anastasia Tsioulcas
item.media:credit: Elias Williams for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jeffrey Zeigler grew up knowing almost nothing about his father’s family. As an undergraduate he visited an older relative who provided him with stories and family lore.

item.title: With ‘Seven Guitars,’ Ruben Santiago-Hudson Keeps the Light on for August Wilson
item.description: Ruben Santiago-Hudson, a recent Tony nominee for “Joe Turner’s Come and Gone,” returns to the director’s chair for this season’s revival of “Seven Guitars.”
item.dc:creator: Helen Shaw and Marcus Maddox
item.media:description: In 1984, Ruben Santiago-Hudson slipped into a Broadway production of Wilson’s “Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom.” It was a revelation, and he recalled thinking: “There’s a place for me!”

item.title: Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After ‘Free Palestine’ Remarks
item.description: The rapper, a critic of the war in Gaza, made the comments onstage at MetLife Stadium.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:credit: Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Macklemore’s 2012 track “Thrift Shop,” released with his former producer Ryan Lewis, helped the duo win four Grammy Awards.

item.title: A Wynton Marsalis Symphony Sees the Potential in America
item.description: This famed trumpeter and composer premiered his Fifth Symphony, “Liberty,” which blends a jazz ensemble and a traditional orchestra.
item.dc:creator: Seth Colter Walls

item.media:description: James Gaffigan leading the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra and the National Symphony Orchestra in the premiere of Wynton Marsalis’s Fifth Symphony at Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts on Saturday.

item.title: San Francisco Opera Cancels Opening Night After Musicians Strike
item.description: The labor action forced the opera to cancel as patrons were finding their seats, and threw the season of one of the nation’s premier companies into limbo.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nagourney
item.media:credit: Kelsey McClellan for The New York Times
item.media:description: The San Francisco Opera says it is struggling with a $15 million shortfall driven by rising costs. The musicians say they need salaries that keep pace with the city’s high cost of living.

item.title: Celine Dion Begins Her Paris Comeback Concert Run
item.description: Her long-awaited concert return highlighted a side of the French-speaking superstar rarely seen in the United States.
